headlines.title: What Bernstein Sees Looming Over ConocoPhillips (COP)
headlines.summary: We just published a list of the Sell Alert: 10 Stocks Analysts Downgraded on Thursday and ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) ranked 7th on this list. Chip stocks took the hardest hit on November 5, when the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumped 12.2%, its biggest one-day drop since April 2025. The S&P 500 slid 4.

headlines.title: A December Rate Hike Looks Likely: Buy These 3 Energy and Materials Dividend Stocks Before the Fed Moves
headlines.summary: Rate hikes usually punish income stocks that lean on cheap debt, but some dividend payers earn their cash from oil wells, pipelines, and copper mines. Three of them cover their payouts in very different ways, and one carries a risk its holders can't hedge.

headlines.title: ConocoPhillips' Lower 48 and Willow Assets: Key to Long-Term Growth?
headlines.summary: COP's deep Lower 48 inventory, Willow project and LNG expansion underpin its long-term growth strategy and $7 billion cash flow inflection target by 2029.

headlines.title: Amazon Joins Goldman Sachs’ Conviction List Alongside 4 Other Stock Picks
headlines.summary: Goldman Sachs just overhauled its Conviction List with five new additions, and the upside targets on some of these picks will raise eyebrows. One hyperscaler alone carries a 51% potential gain, but it is far from the biggest number on the list.

headlines.title: ConocoPhillips (COP) Stock Looks Like A Bargain After Fresh Results
headlines.summary: ConocoPhillips has delivered a powerful run in recent years, and with earnings in focus after fresh results and a higher dividend, the key question is whether the current share price still lines up with what the business is earning. Over the past 5 years the stock has gained 127.4%, which puts real pressure on the idea that its earnings can comfortably carry today's valuation.

description: ConocoPhillips explores for, produces, transports, and markets crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG), and natural gas liquids. It operates in five segments: Alaska; Lower 48; Canada; Europe, Middle East and North Africa; and Asia Pacific. The company's portfolio includes unconventional plays in North America; conventional assets in North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia; global LNG developments; oil sands assets in Canada; and an inventory of global exploration prospects. It serves in the United States, Canada, China, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and internationally. ConocoPhillips was founded in 1917 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
